source_text: Subiunxit in eo regnasse mortem, in quo omnes peccaverunt [n311] , quo sermone non nascentis ruina, sed opera agentis expressa est. Approbavit se itaque pravitatem arguere nec innocentiam sauciare.
pass_a_gloss: He subjoined that death reigned in that in which all sinned, by which speech not a ruin of one being born, but the works of one acting have been expressed. He therefore approved that he accuses crookedness and does not wound innocence.

lemmas.lexica: LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5
LS relative; Rom 5:12 in quo omnes peccaverunt — keep Latin force
LS nascor; Blaise infants in the original-sin debate

pass_b_english: He added that death reigned in that all sinned (Romans 5:12). This expression describes not the ruin of someone being born but the works of someone acting. He thus proved that he accuses perversity and does not wound innocence.

choices.why: Julian: Paul says death passed to all, not sin; distinguish temporal death from eternal punishment.
Julian/Augustine dispute turns on the Latin of Rom 5:12; keep 'in whom' rather than a modern Bible's 'because'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
